# Patrick Koorevaar - Azure DevOps Engineer

## About

Patrick Koorevaar is a senior Azure DevOps Engineer focused on cloud-native infrastructure, DevOps automation, and container orchestration. At Q-Vend B.V. he leads end-to-end Azure infrastructure, automation, and scalable deployments across AKS, ACA, CI/CD, and production platforms. In his side projects, he has built a delivery pipeline in which AI agents do the routine work, with the guardrails in code and the final review his own. Currently studying for the CKA.

Before publishing full projects on GitHub, I spent years helping others on [Stack Overflow](https://stackoverflow.com/users/1122629/patrick-koorevaar): 59 questions answered, 1.4k reputation, mostly C#, Git, and Azure/Kubernetes scenarios.

Every side project starts from "what can the free tiers cover" — Cloudflare Workers AI, Cosmos DB free tier, Container Apps scaled to zero. VS Code for frontend, VS Pro for backends, same split at work and on side projects.

*Production*

### Infrastructure as code

*Production*

Terraform and Bicep, deployed via GitHub Actions with OIDC and least-privilege roles kept out of the CI pipeline by design.

- Tags: Terraform · Bicep

## My work style

### Building with AI, not just prompting it

I build my automation in a back and forth with Claude Code. It proposes the design, writes the code, tests and docs, and asks me numbered questions with a recommendation when a decision is mine. I create what only I can (Cloudflare tokens, GitHub environments and secrets), review every PR, and push back when something doesn't fit. In one day of that loop we built an end to end, AI-operated deployment for client sites: I give Claude a site name and a request, and after my review and merge the pipeline puts it live.

### Agentic backlog management

Ideas and the feature backlog live on a private GitHub Projects board. Claude Code files and updates items directly via the GitHub GraphQL API during planning conversations, capturing decisions and open questions as they're made.

### Blog content pipeline

Posts are written as Markdown, stored in Cosmos DB, served through an ACA API. I ask Claude to insert or update articles directly; deleting a post is deliberately left to me only. A Cloudflare Worker converts Markdown to HTML on the way out.

### Building this website

Started out built with Aider paired with a local Qwen2.5 model running via IPEX Ollama. Ongoing iteration — new sections, project cards, fixes — now runs through Claude Code instead.

### Everyday tool stack

VS Code for frontend work, Visual Studio Pro for backends — the same split at work and on side projects.

- Tags: Work: Azure Repos/DevOps/Registry, AKS · Side projects: GitHub Actions/Registry, ACA

### Cost-conscious architecture

Every side project starts from "what can the free tiers cover" — Cloudflare Workers/DNS/Web Analytics, Cosmos DB free tier, Container Apps scaled to zero, Entra ID plus Cloudflare Zero Trust for auth. Workers AI over Azure AI Foundry for the same reason. Anything bigger runs briefly on the Azure credit from my VS Pro subscription, then gets torn down.
